references.text: Moses designates three cities of refuge east of the Jordan for those who have killed someone accidentally, demonstrating the practical application of the law concerning cities of refuge.
Detailed instructions about cities of refuge in Deuteronomy, including criteria for unintentional killing and protection from the avenger of blood.
Joshua carries out the command to designate cities of refuge in Canaan, naming the six cities that were to serve this purpose.
Hebron is mentioned as one of the cities of refuge given to the descendants of Aaron.
Shechem is mentioned as a city of refuge in the hill country of Ephraim.
Golan in Bashan is mentioned as a city of refuge for the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Kedesh in Galilee is mentioned as a city of refuge for the tribe of Naphtali.
Bezer is mentioned as a city of refuge for the tribe of Reuben.
Ramoth in Gilead is mentioned as a city of refuge for the tribe of Gad.
Early legislation concerning a place of refuge for someone who kills without intent, forming the basis for the system of cities of refuge.
Earlier in the same chapter it is described that six of the Levitical cities are to be cities of refuge.
It clarifies that the cities of refuge were also to apply to foreigners and residents, not only Israelites.
The Epistle to the Hebrews uses the image of refuge as a typology for the salvation we have in Christ, where believers have fled to grasp the hope set before us.
